semantics.out_different: For i=0..2, in[i] XOR in[i+1]; bit 3 is in[3] XOR in[0].
semantics.cycle_reset_initialization: Original interface has no clock or reset and describes input bit relationships directly; no state, cycles, initialization requirement, or added latency.
semantics.unused_outputs: Drive out_both[3] and out_any[0] to zero as deterministic implementation choices; original says these answers are not needed.

numeric.indexing: Higher index is left; lower index is right.
numeric.operators: Bitwise AND, OR, XOR; no arithmetic or signed interpretation.
numeric.four_state: Use normal Verilog bitwise propagation; original specifies binary relationships without an explicit X/Z requirement.

verification.oracle_basis: Original problem text, using individual indexed neighboring bits.
verification.sampling: Allow 1 ns combinational settling after each input change; no clock exists.
verification.unused_bits: Do not assert values of out_both[3] or out_any[0].
verification.additional_cases: All 256 four-state input patterns exercise standard bitwise semantics.
verification.failure: $fatal on mismatch and bounded timeout; print PASS only after all checks.

specification_ambiguities.evidence: The problem says we do not need to know out_both[3] and out_any[0].
specification_ambiguities.resolution: These bits are unconstrained by the original text; assign zero and exclude them from the oracle.

specification_ambiguities.evidence: The problem only describes whether bits are 1 or different.
specification_ambiguities.resolution: Standard bitwise four-state behavior is an implementation choice; binary exhaustive verification covers explicit requirements.
